title: "Expression Correlation with Logrank Cut-offs"
author:

---

Two immune-marker genes, one figure: the **CD274 (PD-L1) vs CD8A scatter** carries their correlation with a regression confidence band, the patient's MSI status as point shapes, and — on the margins — the **log-rank score curve for every candidate expression cut-off**, whose peak (blue arrow) defines the survival-optimal four-quadrant grouping (I–IV) with population percentages \[1\]. This reproduces Fig. 1C of the colorectal immune-overdrive study \[2\] on simulated data:

## Example

![](../images/SurvCorPlot_demo.png){fig-alt="Expression Correlation with Logrank Cut-offs DEMO" fig-align="center" width="60%"}

## Setup

-   System Requirements: Cross-platform (Linux/MacOS/Windows)

-   Programming language: R

-   Dependent packages: `survival`; `shape`; `ggplot2`

```{r packages setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, output=FALSE}
if (!requireNamespace("shape", quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("shape", repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(ggplot2)
})
```

```{r}
sessioninfo::session_info("attached")
```

## Data Preparation

280 simulated tumours: CD274 and CD8A log2 expression correlated through a latent immune-activity factor, MSI status for a minority, and survival times with planted biology — CD8A-high tumours do better, PD-L1-high/CD8A-low (the immunosuppressed quadrant) worst — so the logrank score peaks sit inside the data range:

```{r load data}
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(survival))
set.seed(14301)
n <- 280
z1 <- rnorm(n)                                   # latent immune activity
CD274 <- round(2.2 + 0.9 * z1 + rnorm(n, 0, 1.1), 2)
CD8A  <- round(0.5 * z1 + rnorm(n, 0, 1.5) + 0.4 * (CD274 > 3), 2)
msi <- sample(n, 40)
expr <- data.frame(CD274 = CD274, CD8A = CD8A, row.names = sprintf("S%03d", 1:n))
## planted biology: CD8A-high tumours do better; PD-L1-high/CD8A-low
## (immunosuppressed quadrant II) do worst -> interior logrank peaks
haz <- exp(0.15 * scale(CD274)[, 1] - 0.55 * (CD8A > 0.5) +
           0.45 * (CD274 > 2 & CD8A <= 0.5))
surv <- data.frame(OS.time = pmin(2400, pmax(30, qweibull(runif(n), 1, 900 / haz))),
                   OS = rbinom(n, 1, 0.55), row.names = rownames(expr))
exprsurv <- cbind.data.frame(surv, expr)
```

## Visualization

### 1. Scatter + Marginal Logrank-Score Strips

The `layout()` composite: top and right strips show the log-rank U statistic for every candidate cut-point of CD274 and CD8A (rect bars), blue arrows flag the survival-optimal peaks; in the scatter, blue dashed lines apply those cut-points (grey dashed = medians), quadrant labels I–IV carry population percentages, and the shaded band is the regression 95% CI:

```{r}
#| label: fig-1.1SurvCor
#| fig-cap: "CD274 vs CD8A expression scatter (simulated) with MSI/MSS point shapes, median and survival-optimal cut-off lines, regression with 95% CI, quadrant percentages I-IV, and marginal log-rank score strips whose peaks (arrows) pick the cut-offs."
#| out.width: "85%"
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| fig-width: 7.2
#| fig-height: 7.2

suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(shape))   # Arrows()
## log-rank score for every candidate cutpoint — dependency-free
## reimplementation of survMisc::cutp: the score is the survdiff chi-square of
## the high/low split at each unique expression value; the peak marks the
## survival-optimal cut-off (on real data survMisc::cutp(coxph) gives the
## same curve on the U-statistic scale)
logrank_curve <- function(gene) {
  vals <- sort(unique(exprsurv[[gene]]))
  vals <- vals[-length(vals)]                # last value would leave an empty group
  score <- vapply(vals, function(v) {
    grp <- exprsurv[[gene]] > v
    survdiff(Surv(OS.time, OS) ~ grp, data = exprsurv)$chisq
  }, numeric(1))
  data.frame(cut = vals, score = score)
}
lr.CD274 <- logrank_curve("CD274")
peak.CD274 <- lr.CD274$cut[which.max(lr.CD274$score)]
peak.CD274.score <- max(lr.CD274$score)
lr.CD8A <- logrank_curve("CD8A")
peak.CD8A <- lr.CD8A$cut[which.max(lr.CD8A$score)]
peak.CD8A.score <- max(lr.CD8A$score)

## quadrant percentages (peak-based grouping, I-IV naming as the paper)
lefttop.pct <- paste0("III (", round(sum(expr$CD274 < peak.CD274 & expr$CD8A > peak.CD8A) / n, 2) * 100, "%)")
leftbottom.pct <- paste0("I (", round(sum(expr$CD274 <= peak.CD274 & expr$CD8A <= peak.CD8A) / n, 2) * 100, "%)")
righttop.pct <- paste0("IV (", round(sum(expr$CD274 >= peak.CD274 & expr$CD8A >= peak.CD8A) / n, 2) * 100, "%)")
rightbottom.pct <- paste0("II (", round(sum(expr$CD274 > peak.CD274 & expr$CD8A < peak.CD8A) / n, 2) * 100, "%)")

cor <- cor.test(expr$CD274, expr$CD8A, method = "pearson")
r <- round(cor$estimate, 2)
p <- ifelse(cor$p.value < 0.001, " < 0.001", paste0(" = ", round(cor$p.value, 3)))
reg <- lm(CD8A ~ CD274, data = expr[order(expr$CD274), ])
ci <- as.data.frame(predict(reg, newdata = expr[order(expr$CD274), ], interval = "confidence"))

blue <- "#4F81BD"; red <- "#E53435"; lblue <- "#5bc0eb"; dblue <- "#1d00ff"; pink <- "#FF7FBF"
ylim <- range(expr$CD8A); xlim <- range(expr$CD274)
layout(matrix(c(1,1,1,1,2,
                3,3,3,3,4,
                3,3,3,3,4,
                3,3,3,3,4,
                3,3,3,3,4), byrow = TRUE, nrow = 5))
## area 1: x-gene logrank scores
par(bty = "n", mgp = c(2, 0.5, 0), mar = c(0.6, 4.1, 2.1, 0), tcl = -0.25, xpd = TRUE)
plot(NULL, NULL, xlim = xlim, ylim = c(0, max(lr.CD274$score) + 5),
     xaxt = "n", yaxt = "n", ann = FALSE)
rect(lr.CD274$cut - 0.012, 0, lr.CD274$cut + 0.012, lr.CD274$score, col = "black")
Arrows(peak.CD274, peak.CD274.score + 5, peak.CD274, peak.CD274.score + 3,
       arr.length = 0.2, lwd = 2, col = blue, arr.type = "triangle")
## area 2: spacer
par(bty = "n", mar = c(4.1, 4.1, 0, 0))
plot(0, 0, col = "white", xaxt = "n", yaxt = "n", xlab = "", ylab = "")
## area 3: main scatter
par(bty = "o", mgp = c(2, 0.5, 0), mar = c(4.1, 4.1, 0, 0), tcl = -0.25,
    font.axis = 2, las = 1); par(xpd = FALSE)
mss.sam <- setdiff(rownames(expr), sprintf("S%03d", msi))
msi.sam <- sprintf("S%03d", msi)
plot(expr[mss.sam, "CD274"], expr[mss.sam, "CD8A"], ylim = ylim, xlim = xlim,
     xlab = expression(italic(CD274) ~ "(PD-L1) Gene Expression"),
     ylab = expression(italic(CD8A) ~ " Gene Expression"),
     cex.lab = 1.3, cex.axis = 1.1, col = "grey40", cex = 1.0, pch = 19)
points(expr[msi.sam, "CD274"], expr[msi.sam, "CD8A"], col = "black", cex = 1.6, pch = 17)
abline(h = median(expr$CD8A), lty = 2, col = "grey60", lwd = 2)
abline(v = median(expr$CD274), lty = 2, col = "grey60", lwd = 2)
abline(v = peak.CD274, lty = 2, col = blue, lwd = 2)
abline(h = peak.CD8A, lty = 2, col = blue, lwd = 2)
polygon(round(c(sort(expr$CD274), rev(sort(expr$CD274))), 2),
        round(c(ci$lwr, rev(ci$upr)), 2), col = adjustcolor("grey70", 0.6), border = NA)
lines(x = xlim, y = xlim * reg$coefficients[2] + reg$coefficients[1], lwd = 2)
xmin <- par("usr")[1]; xmax <- par("usr")[2]; ymin <- par("usr")[3]; ymax <- par("usr")[4]
text(xmin + 0.2, ymin + 0.45, adj = 0,
     bquote(~italic(r) ~ " = " ~ .(r) ~ ", " ~ italic(P) ~ .(p)), cex = 1.2)
text(xmin + (peak.CD274 - xmin) / 2, ymin + (peak.CD8A - ymin) / 2,
     bquote(bold(.(leftbottom.pct))), cex = 1.3, col = lblue)
text(peak.CD274 + (xmax - peak.CD274) / 2, ymin + (peak.CD8A - ymin) / 2,
     bquote(bold(.(rightbottom.pct))), cex = 1.3, col = pink)
text(xmin + (peak.CD274 - xmin) / 2, peak.CD8A + (ymax - peak.CD8A) / 2,
     bquote(bold(.(lefttop.pct))), cex = 1.3, col = dblue)
text(peak.CD274 + (xmax - peak.CD274) / 2, peak.CD8A + (ymax - peak.CD8A) / 2,
     bquote(bold(.(righttop.pct))), cex = 1.3, col = red)
legend("bottomright", legend = c("MSI", "MSS"), col = c("black", "grey40"),
       pch = c(17, 19), cex = 1.1, title = expression(bold("MSI Status")),
       bty = "o", xpd = TRUE, inset = c(0, -0.02))
## area 4: y-gene logrank scores
par(bty = "n", mgp = c(2, 0.5, 0), mar = c(4.1, 0.6, 0, 2.1), tcl = -0.25, xpd = TRUE)
plot(NULL, NULL, xlim = c(0, max(lr.CD8A$score) + 5), ylim = ylim,
     xaxt = "n", yaxt = "n", ann = FALSE)
rect(0, lr.CD8A$cut - 0.03, lr.CD8A$score, lr.CD8A$cut + 0.03, col = "black")
Arrows(peak.CD8A.score + 5, peak.CD8A, peak.CD8A.score + 3, peak.CD8A,
       arr.length = 0.2, lwd = 2, col = blue, arr.type = "triangle")
```

::: callout-tip
**Practice tips**

-   `survMisc::cutp()` on a `coxph` fit scores **every unique expression value** as a candidate cut-point; the peak of the U curve is the survival-optimal split — but with no multiplicity correction this is the definition of an *optimized* cut-off, so say so in the caption.
-   The quadrant membership test uses **different inequalities on each side** (`<` vs `<=`) so boundary samples are counted once; re-check percentages sum to 100%.
-   A secondary peak in the marginal score curve (as in the reference's CD274 for CRC) can flag a subgroup with reversed survival — scan the whole curve, not just its maximum.
:::

## Applications

::: {#fig-SurvCorApplications1}
![](../images/SurvCorPlot_demo.png){fig-alt="Correlation + survival-optimal cut-offs" fig-align="center" width="60%"}

Correlation + survival-optimal cut-offs

The scatter + marginal-score layout fits any two-marker immune or pathway pair where both axes need survival-optimal stratification: PD-1 vs CTLA4, proliferation vs immune score, or risk scores from two models.

\[2\] Fakih M, Ouyang C, Wang C, et al. Immune overdrive signature in colorectal tumor subset predicts poor clinical outcome. J Clin Invest. 2019;129(10):4464-4476. doi:10.1172/JCI127046
